title: Melic label, Ethel Waters search, and the Damita Jo album
summary: Lee started Melic with publishing companies Flipside and Land Lee, considered recording Ethel Waters, and made an album with Damita Jo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: That's right, called me once and
That was when you were looking for Ethel Waters. And we found her in Pasadena.
That's right. And so I started Melic record label, and I had 2 publishing companies; one in BMI called Flipside and the other in ASCAP called Land Lee. Well, I recorded some people.

You know, speaking of Ethel Waters, I thought -- my thing about looking for Ethel Waters at the time, I thought it would be a good idea, because I'll tell you, my first time away from home, I went away from home with here, and I thought in my mind it would be a good thing to get here and record her. But after I -- I did find her in Pasadena, incidentally -- after I went out and talked to her, then I began to learn a little more about the record business, and I knew it would not be a good idea to record her, so instead of her, I found Damita Jo, and I did an album on Damita Jo.
She sang at the Oasis when your band was there, didn't she?

No. No. She was at the [Belle Tavern.] See, she was at the [Belle Tavern] when Ernie was there -- Marshall's brother -- Ernie Royal. That was her first job. She auditioned, when she was like, 18 years old -- from Santa Barbara. But no, she didn't do the Oasis with me. I made an album with her and Dave Grusin did the arrangements.

And that was in '63. I didn't know anything about the record business at all -- was scared to death. Twentieth Century Fox wanted to give me $20,000 advance for the album, and I wouldn't take it because I thought they were going to ...
